intro: Office clerks build coordination, time management and service skills that administrative and billing teams count on. Of the 25 careers below, the closest match for office clerks is Secretaries and Administrative Assistants at 95%, and 19 of the 25 pay more than the $45,010 median.
why_it_works: Office clerks keep records straight, answer questions and handle a steady flow of small tasks without dropping any. O*NET rates coordination, time management and service orientation at 3 out of 5 for this job, so assistant, billing and records roles rank very high. Many use the same software and filing habits with more responsibility. Bookkeeping and executive assistant roles pay more for that same accuracy. The skills to build are operations analysis and problem solving.
tips: Ask to take on billing, scheduling or reporting tasks, since those lead to the better-paid matches.
Learn spreadsheets well; bookkeeping and administrative roles use them every day.
Look at executive assistant roles if you want a big pay step without a four-year degree.

faq.q: What jobs can office clerks move into?
faq.a: The closest matches are Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive (95%), File Clerks (93%) and Correspondence Clerks (91%), based on O*NET 31.0. Billing and Posting Clerks (90%) and Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants (89%) are also close.

faq.q: Which jobs pay more than office clerk?
faq.a: 19 of the 25 matches pay more than the $45,010 median for office clerks. Administrative Services Managers earn $114,130 (+154%), Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants earn $76,590 (+70%) and Brokerage Clerks earn $65,750 (+46%), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do office clerks need a degree to move up?
faq.a: Not for most options. 17 of the 25 matches usually need no more education than an office clerk job, based on O*NET Job Zones. The others usually need a certificate or associate degree, including bookkeeping clerks and executive assistants.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to office clerk?
faq.a: In the same field, the nearest roles are Word Processors and Typists (86% match), Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks (84%) and Data Entry Keyers (82%). Claims processing is often the better move, since it builds on clerk work and adds insurance knowledge.
